title: Mid Cabin Lavatory Out of Service on Long Cold Sectors — Amaranth Airways
abstract: Amaranth Airways reports the mid cabin lavatories going out of service late in long northern sectors, restored only after the aircraft has been on the ground and warm for some hours, with passenger complaints concentrated on the affected rotations.

sections.request: On our long northern rotations the two mid cabin lavatories stop flushing about eight hours in, always the same two, always after a long cruise segment at high latitude. The cabin crew get a service message and the units come back by themselves once the aeroplane has been on stand for a few hours in the warm. Our engineers can never reproduce it on the ground. We are getting written complaints on those flights because it leaves the rear of the aeroplane with too few working lavatories for the passenger load. We would like this fixed properly rather than deferred every time.
sections.background: The units have been changed twice on one airframe with no improvement, so we stopped changing them. Our cabin log data shows twenty-two events on eleven rotations over one winter, all on sectors longer than nine hours routed above sixty degrees north, and none on our southern network. A line engineer has suggested the run under the floor at that station is the coldest part of the system, but we have nothing in writing about that.
sections.expected_outcome: Two mid cabin lavatories that work for the whole sector on our northern network, without a deferral, and without the cabin crew having to manage passengers around them. If a heater or a lagging change is needed we would rather take the downtime once than carry this every winter.

type_data.business_justification: Twenty-two events in one winter on eleven rotations, sixty-one written passenger complaints and two goodwill compensations. The operator carries a standing deferral it considers unacceptable on a premium long haul product.
